titulo: Expanded Longitudinal Validation of Adaptive Learning Stability in AI-Assisted Neurosurgical Residency Training
tituloEs: Inteligencia artificial estabiliza trayectorias de competencia en residencia de neurocirugía
resumenOriginal:
Objective: To evaluate the longitudinal stability, reproducibility, and robustness of Adaptive Learning Stability (ALS) within an expanded AI-assisted neurosurgical residency cohort during a 12-month observation cycle.

Design: This was a prospective controlled educational study. Residents completed 4 consecutive quarterly checkpoints integrating cognitive, technical, and decision-making assessments over 12 months. The RCKaS-AI framework incorporated predictive analytics, individualized adaptive remediation, and mentor-validated feedback pathways. Primary analysis evaluated longitudinal entrustment trajectory stability across checkpoints. Secondary analyses included inter-resident variance dynamics, remediation frequency, faculty workload, and predictive agreement between forecasted and observed competency progression.

Setting: Two accredited neurosurgical residency programs in Kazakhstan, from January 2025 to January 2026.

Participants: Sixty-four neurosurgical residents randomized into standard RCKaS (n = 32) and AI-enhanced RCKaS-AI (n = 32) cohorts.

Results: Both cohorts demonstrated progressive improvement in entrustment scores across sequential checkpoints. In the RCKaS-AI cohort, mean entrustment scores increased from 59.1 ± 12.8 at CP1 to 94.3 ± 6.9 at CP4, compared with 58.4 ± 13.1 to 85.7 ± 10.4 under standard RCKaS conditions (p = 0.001). Inter-resident variance decreased by 41% in the AI-assisted cohort versus 18% in the standard cohort. Residents within the RCKaS-AI framework achieved entrustment level 4 significantly earlier than controls (38 ± 7 weeks vs 50 ± 9 weeks, p = 0.003). Mean remediation frequency decreased from 3.4 ± 1.1 to 1.9 ± 0.7 sessions per resident, while faculty workload declined by 34%. Predictive analytics demonstrated strong agreement between forecasted and observed competency trajectories (r = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.77-0.89).

Conclusions: Expanded longitudinal implementation of the RCKaS-AI framework demonstrated reproducible stabilization of competency trajectories during neurosurgical residency training. These findings support the robustness of adaptive AI-assisted feedback systems as a practical mechanism for longitudinal competency regulation within structured surgical education programs. Further multicenter validation is required to evaluate external reproducibility across broader residency environments.

tips.texto: Implementen checkpoints cada 3 meses integrando evaluación cognitiva, técnica y toma de decisiones. Esta estructura permite detectar trayectorias atípicas tempranamente.
Registren dispersión de desempeño entre residentes del mismo nivel. Variabilidad decreciente indica que el sistema formativo está funcionando equitativamente.
Si usan herramientas digitales, verifiquen concordancia entre pronóstico y desempeño real trimestre a trimestre. Ajusten umbrales si la correlación cae bajo 0.75.
Diseñen planes correctivos basados en déficits específicos del residente, no protocolos genéricos. Esto redujo sesiones remediales de 3.4 a 1.9 por residente.
Midan semanas desde ingreso hasta nivel de confianza 4. Este indicador objetivo revela si el sistema acelera o retrasa competencia independiente.

sintesis: Estudio controlado con 64 residentes de neurocirugía comparó formación estándar versus sistema asistido por IA durante 12 meses. El grupo con IA logró competencia confiable 12 semanas antes, redujo variabilidad entre residentes 41% y disminuyó carga docente 34%.
aplicacionDocente: Estructuren evaluación longitudinal con puntos de corte trimestrales que integren dominios múltiples. Registren dispersión de desempeño grupal como indicador de equidad formativa. Si implementan sistemas digitales de retroalimentación, validen su capacidad predictiva comparando pronósticos con desempeño observado cada trimestre.
disenoEstudio: Ensayo controlado prospectivo con 64 residentes de neurocirugía, seguimiento trimestral durante 12 meses
fraseInfografia: Sistema con IA acelera 12 semanas la autonomía quirúrgica y reduce 34% carga docente
advertencia: Estudio realizado en dos programas de un solo país; reproducibilidad en contextos culturales y estructurales distintos requiere validación multicéntrica.
